key_insight: In high-entropy fluorite oxides, Np/Am short-range ordering creates lattice distortion that first suppresses O-ion motion, then reorganizes into interconnected pathways that trigger a superionic transition and can even reverse the mobility ranking relative to random solid solutions.
engineering_relevance: These results help guide the design of advanced nuclear fuel ceramics by showing how local chemical ordering can be tuned to balance radiation tolerance with fast oxygen transport under extreme temperatures.
method: Hybrid Monte Carlo / Molecular Dynamics simulations
Compare short-range ordered (SRO) and random solid solution (RSS) models across 2000–2800 K
Analyze diffusion, lattice distortion, Gibbs free energy, and defect evolution
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a temperature-dependent kinetic inversion, with a Tammann crossover and superionic transition separating low-mobility trapped-ion behavior from a high-mobility, entropy-driven transport regime.
watch_item: The conclusions are simulation-based and may depend on the chosen force model, composition, and temperature window, so experimental validation is needed before materials deployment.
paper_title: Interplay between high-entropy effects and the superionic transition in fluorite oxides: A liquid-like perspective
